title: Instructional Design Checkpoint Navigator
description: A Mermaid flowchart of the instructional design checkpoint with a click directive on every node that opens its definition and an example. A Try a specification mode loads one of four sample MicroSim specifications, lets the learner click the path they would take through the four checkpoint questions, compares it with the recommended path, and displays the completed Instructional Design Check block.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Educational Technology
Instructional Design
Bloom's Taxonomy
MicroSim Engineering

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
learningObjectives: The learner will execute the instructional design checkpoint on a supplied MicroSim specification, reaching a recorded decision about interaction pattern, prediction and animation.
prerequisites: Intrinsic, extraneous and germane cognitive load

accessibility.notes: Node text is real HTML inside the SVG; the information panel is plain HTML.

controls.label: Check my path
controls.action: Compare the clicked path with the recommended path and show the decision block

controls.label: Any node
controls.action: Show the node's definition and example, or add it to the path in Try mode

assumptions: Recommended paths follow the four checkpoint questions as described in Chapter 3 and the generator skill's Step 3.
limitations: The comparison is position by position; it reports the first step where the paths differ.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Guided practice on worked cases with immediate comparison
keyQuestions: What concrete data must the learner see?
Does the learner need to predict before observing?
Can you finish the sentence 'the animation shows ___, which an arrow cannot'?
Is continuous animation appropriate for this Bloom level?
commonMisconceptions: If the phenomenon moves, continuous animation is always appropriate.
A step-through means the MicroSim has no animation at all.
The checkpoint is optional when the specification is detailed.
assessmentOpportunities: Path accuracy on the four samples
Learner-written decision blocks compared with the completed ones
